text:
Florida won 7-3, but if every shot in this game were replayed, Columbus would have come out ahead slightly more often than not (51 percent to 49). The Blue Jackets generated more quality at even strength (2.57 expected goals to 2.10) and dominated the first period, outchancing the Panthers 1.80 to 0.55 and getting a Kent Johnson goal for a 1-0 lead. What the metrics can't fully excuse is what came next: Columbus took six penalties' worth of trouble, 25 penalty minutes in all, and Florida turned the extra skaters into the game.

The second period was the Panthers' penalty-fueled stretch. Brady Tkachuk scored three times, two of them on the power play, the first a tip-in and the second a wrist shot that carried a 30 percent chance of scoring, one of the better looks of the night. Matthew Tkachuk assisted on all of them and finished with five helpers, while Seth Jones added four. Carter Verhaeghe made it 4-1 on another power play, and Sam Reinhart's tip-in early in the third made it 5-1. Florida went 4 for 6 with the man advantage, and Cam Talbot allowed 6 goals on 2.52 expected, a gap of about three and a half goals.

Columbus did not quit. Denton Mateychuk and Cole Sillinger scored 22 seconds apart in the third to cut it to 6-3, and Jet Greaves stopped all four shots he saw in relief. But Reinhart's second goal, a 57 percent chance, closed it out. The Blue Jackets played the game on roughly even terms, and the penalty box made the scoreboard look nothing like it.
